title: Surjective restrictions on quasi-compact opens imply acyclicity
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space whose quasi-compact open subsets form a basis and whose intersections of two quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X$. Suppose that $G(V)\to G(U)$ is surjective whenever $U\subseteq V$ are quasi-compact opens. Then for every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$ and every integer $q>0$, $H^q(V,G|_V)=0$, using right-derived global sections of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Here $G|_V$ is the ordinary restriction of the sheaf to the open subspace $V$. Neither quasi-compactness of $X$ nor a Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0A36 (lemma-vanishing-ravi) and 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis), applied to the basis of quasi-compact opens and all its finite covers; this is the acyclicity argument used in Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, proof of (1) assuming (2).

proof.text: Fix a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$ and put $F=G|_V$, so $F(W)=G(W)$ for each open $W\subseteq V$. Work on the open site of the subspace $V$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal B_V$ be the opens of $V$ whose images are quasi-compact opens of $X$, including $\varnothing$. These form a basis: an open of $V$ is open in $X$, so each of its points has a quasi-compact open neighbourhood contained in it. Let $\mathrm{Cov}_V$ consist of all finite covers $W=\bigcup_{i\in I}W_i$ with $W,W_i\in\mathcal B_V$, using finite ordinal index sets (including the empty one). This is a set of covers. Given any open cover of $W\in\mathcal B_V$, choose for every point a basis neighbourhood contained in a cover member and then take a finite subcover by quasi-compactness of $W$. Thus $\mathrm{Cov}_V$ is cofinal among covers of every $W\in\mathcal B_V$. For $W=\varnothing$ the empty cover gives the same refinement statement.

source.place: Tag 01EW, lemma-cech-vanish-basis, hypotheses (1)-(2); Tag 0A3G, proof of (1) assuming (2), finite coverings by quasi-compact opens

proof.text: For a cover $\mathcal W=(W_i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathrm{Cov}_V$, every nonempty finite intersection $W_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}W_j$ is a quasi-compact open of $X$, by induction using the pairwise-intersection hypothesis. In particular all tuple intersections, with repetitions allowed, belong to $\mathcal B_V$. There are only finitely many nonempty subsets of the finite set $I$. Hence an arbitrary union $W_{\mathcal S}=\bigcup_{J\in\mathcal S}W_J$ of these intersections is a finite union of quasi-compact opens, and is quasi-compact: for any open cover take a finite subcover on each of the finitely many pieces and join these subcovers. The empty union is quasi-compact as well. Since $W_{\mathcal S}\subseteq W$ and both are quasi-compact opens in $X$, the hypothesis on $G$ gives a surjection $F(W)=G(W)\longrightarrow G(W_{\mathcal S})=F(W_{\mathcal S})$.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proof of (1) assuming (2), verification of the hypotheses of Tag 0A36 for finite quasi-compact-open covers

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cech-vanishing-surjective-unions] to the topological space $V$, its abelian sheaf $F$, and each cover $\mathcal W\in\mathrm{Cov}_V$. Step 2 verifies surjectivity for every union of its finite nonempty intersections, not merely for individual intersections. We obtain $\check H^p(\mathcal W,F)=0$ for every $p>0$ and every such finite cover, with the ordinary ordered-tuple Cech complex.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi; applied as in Tag 0A3G, proof of (1) assuming (2)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to the open site of $V$, $\mathcal B_V$, $\mathrm{Cov}_V$ and $F$. Its condition (1) holds by the finite-intersection calculation of Step 2, condition (2) by the cofinality proof in Step 1, and condition (3) by Step 3. It follows that $R^q\Gamma(W,-)(F)=0$ for every $q>0$ and $W\in\mathcal B_V$. In particular $V\in\mathcal B_V$ by the chosen quasi-compactness of $V$. On its open site, evaluation at the terminal open $V$ is global sections of abelian sheaves on $V$; by [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] its right derived groups are precisely $H^q(V,G|_V)$. This proves the assertion for every quasi-compact open $V$. The same argument includes the empty space and empty open; no compactness of $X$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-9cd39d6d5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the one new node lem-sfb-cech-vanishing-surjective-unions, and all cited statements in full: def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex, def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology, lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion (03F9). The new node states exactly Stacks 0A36 (cohomology.tex lemma-vanishing-ravi, statement and proof checked): taking unions over families of finite nonempty J ⊆ I gives the same opens as unions of tuple intersections. The empty family is harmless, and no finiteness or separation hypothesis is added. The node is not a clause of the item and duplicates nothing: rg -L for 0A36, 0A3G, flasque and unions of intersections finds only the parent sfb nodes, the Noetherian pbc top-degree nodes and lem-sc-topological-flasque-acyclic, which needs full flasqueness. The item proof follows the 0A3G proof of (1) from (2). Step 1: the qc opens of X inside V form a basis B_V, and finite ordinal-indexed covers in B_V are cofinal (pointwise basis refinement plus a finite subcover), giving 03F9(2). Step 2: finite intersections are qc by pairwise stability, so 03F9(1) holds, and with finitely many J any union W_S is a finite union of qc opens, hence qc and inside W, so the hypothesis on G gives surjectivity. Step 3: the new node gives Čech vanishing, 03F9(3). Step 4: 03F9 on the open site of V, with V in B_V, and def-sc identifies R^qΓ(V,-) with H^q(V,G|_V), so no restriction comparison is hidden. Tested on Z on an irreducible spectral space, discrete spaces, empty V and empty covers, and Z on S^1 with two arcs (the new node's hypothesis correctly fails there). Accepted the declared tool_use of lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion as a generic black box that realises the prescribed 01EW step. No SGA is cited. review_split.py reports 'no such node' for four cited ids, but all of them exist through the symlinked chapter directories, so this is a tooling artefact. No changes made.
